finding.claim: Urlencoded request bodies whose Content-Type carries parameters (e.g. charset=UTF-8) are never parsed by default, so ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY stay empty and body rules miss payloads.
finding.source: HTTP client POST with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8 (unauthenticated)
finding.sink: Body processor selection for ARGS_POST / REQUEST_BODY (transaction.go:1100-1120, urlencoded.go:26-31)

trace.note: Exact equality match against application/x-www-form-urlencoded; parameterized value does not match, reqbodyProcessor left empty
URLENCODED default applies only when ForceRequestBodyVariable is set
rbp empty: evaluates PhaseRequestBody without parsing the body
ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults to false per transaction
Only code path that fills ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY is never reached

finding.guards_checked: Exact-match content-type gate is the only selector; ForceRequestBodyVariable default off; no fallback parser; ctl:requestBodyProcessor/forceRequestBodyVariable require a ruleset to set them. Not verified: whether CRS forces URLENCODED for these content types.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI fails on the request target, the query string is never extracted into ARGS_GET, so query payloads are invisible to argument rules while still present in REQUEST_URI_RAW.
finding.source: HTTP request line with an invalid percent-escape in the path, e.g. GET /a%zz?q=<payload> (unauthenticated)

trace.note: Error branch: sets urlencodedError and path=uri only
Query extraction for the error branch is commented out
ExtractGetArguments only called in the success branch (sole caller)

finding.guards_checked: urlencodedError is set (transaction.go:837) but not enforced by the engine; it only helps if a rule checks URLENCODED_ERROR, which was not verified.

finding.claim: The request target is truncated at the first '#' before parsing, so query parameters after a raw '#' are missing from ARGS_GET even though backends that do not treat '#' as a fragment receive them.
finding.source: Raw request line GET /p?a=1#&b=<payload> HTTP/1.1 from a non-browser client

trace.note: strings.Index(uri, "#") truncates the URI before parsing
ExtractGetArguments receives a query without b=<payload>

finding.guards_checked: No control on this path; REQUEST_URI_RAW (line 822) keeps the full string. Backend-side behavior (Go net/http keeps '#' in RawQuery; PHP) is from stdlib knowledge, not verified in this repo.

finding.claim: JSON flattening writes every key into one map keyed by dotted path, so a literal key 'a.b' and nested a->b collide and the later value silently overwrites the earlier one, hiding it from inspection.
finding.source: JSON body such as {"a.b":"<payload>","a":{"b":"x"}} (unauthenticated, when the ruleset enables ctl:requestBodyProcessor=JSON)

trace.note: gjson ForEach walks object keys in order
Nested object recursed into with the same res map
res[objKey] = val overwrites an existing flattened key
Final map copied into ARGS_POST via SetIndex(key,0,value), which also overwrites index 0

finding.guards_checked: No collision detection; JSON processor only runs when a ruleset sets requestBodyProcessor=JSON (default off).
